![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14274602/assets/d0e8cc7d5f289d2bfaa33a21347b4ee60c1e89b58eb0076003d5f37c2ab9e1a8.png)

Consider a continuous function $f$ defined on the closed interval $-8\le x\le 5.$ The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above for the region $-5\le x\le 5,$ and consists of two line segments and an arc of a quarter circle centered at $(0,0)$ with radius $2.$ It is known that the point $(-1,-\sqrt{3})$ is on the graph of $f.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of a circle is

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}.
$$

Substituting the radius $r=2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The graph consists of $4$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-2],$ the arc of the quarter circle for $x\in [-2,0]\,,$ the line segment for $x\in [0,\frac{5}{2}]\,,$ and the line segment for $x\in [\frac{5}{2},5]\,.$
Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{5/2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{5/2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,0]\,.$ The corresponding region is a quarter circle. In part 1, we found the area of the circle as $A=4\pi .$ So we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}A \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4\pi  \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,\frac{5}{2}]\,.$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [\frac{5}{2},5]\,.$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{5}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+(-{A}_{2})+(-{A}_{3})+{A}_{4} \\  & =3-\pi -\frac{5}{2}+\frac{5}{2} \\  & =3-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
